li.label: learning to shoot
li.description: They let me shoot a real weapon! It's heavier than it looks, and I nearly hit the target.

li.label: a child with a weapon
li.description: The council let a child carry a loaded weapon. I've started walking behind things.

li.label: told I'm too little
li.description: The grown-ups said I'm too little to go hunting. I'm not little.

li.label: went out with the hunters
li.description: I got to go out with the hunters and carry the bag. It was heavy and it smelled. Best day ever.

li.label: minding a child on the hunt
li.description: I spent the whole hunt telling a child to stay down and keep quiet. We didn't catch a thing.

li.label: proved them wrong
li.description: They said I was too little to hunt, but I shot a squirrel all by myself.

li.label: taught a kid to shoot
li.description: I taught a kid to shoot today. They held it all wrong and still hit the target. I may have cheered.

li.label: saw what hunting really is
li.description: I watched them gut the animal, and there was so much more inside it than I thought. I want to grow potatoes now.

li.label: the dead go somewhere nice
li.description: They told me the dead go somewhere warm, with good food and no raiders. I asked if there are dogs. They said probably.

li.label: fairy tales for children
li.description: We told a child the dead go somewhere nice. I don't like lying to children.

li.label: learned about the worms
li.description: They told me the worms eat all of you when you're buried, even the eyes. I asked about the eyes specifically.

li.label: my worm collection
li.description: I keep a jar of worms by my bed now. I've given them all names.

li.label: a funeral for a little thing
li.description: We gave a tiny dead animal a proper funeral today, with speeches. I cried a bit.

li.label: time wasted on nonsense
li.description: Work stopped in the middle of the day so people could stand around making speeches. The fields still need weeding.

li.label: nobody would answer me
li.description: I asked one simple question and every grown-up suddenly had somewhere else to be.

li.label: questions about death at breakfast
li.description: The child keeps asking me where the dead go, at every meal. I don't know what to say.

li.label: my friend past the wall
li.description: The animal past the wall eats out of my hand now. It has a name, and I'm not telling you what it is.

li.label: they chased my friend away
li.description: They chased my animal friend away. I still put food out every night, but it doesn't come.

li.label: they killed my friend
li.description: They killed the animal that used to eat out of my hand. I know who did it, and I won't forget.

li.label: feeding the wildlife
li.description: A child keeps carrying our food out past the wall to feed a wild animal. One day it'll come looking for more.

li.label: bitten again
li.description: That animal bit me again, on my other hand this time. The council still won't do anything about it.

li.label: my animal is fading
li.description: Every morning it takes a little longer to get up. I sit with it. I don't know what else to do.

li.label: took my animal on a last walk
li.description: I took my old animal out past the walls, slowly, the long way round. I came back alone.

li.label: nursing my animal
li.description: We've been giving my animal soft food and a warm corner to sleep in. It's eating again.

li.label: dinner got away
li.description: The animal we were going to eat got over the wall and away. I already had the water boiling.

li.label: apologized to an animal
li.description: The council made me apologize to an animal while the others watched. It licked itself the whole time.

li.label: my love letter was read aloud
li.description: I wrote it at three in the morning, and it was read out at dinner, with voices. I wish I'd never written it.

li.label: said it out loud
li.description: I stood on a chair and read my love letter aloud. My knees shook the whole time, but I did it.

li.label: a love letter, read from a chair
li.description: One of us stood on a chair and read a love letter aloud at dinner. It was sweet.

li.label: my coffin is ready
li.description: My coffin is finished and standing in the corner of my room. I check the fit some evenings.

li.label: a coffin in the house
li.description: One of us keeps an empty coffin in their room. It gives me the creeps.

li.label: heard my own eulogies
li.description: They stood up one by one and said kind things about me, while I was alive to hear them. I had no idea they felt that way.

li.label: an honest eulogy
li.description: At my living funeral, one of them stood up and listed everything wrong with me. It was the longest speech of the night.

li.label: picked my grave
li.description: I picked out my grave, out of the wind with a view of the fields. I lay down in it to check.

li.label: bolted in at night
li.description: They bolt my door from the outside at night because I sleepwalk. I feel like a prisoner.

li.label: wearing a bell
li.description: They put a bell on my ankle so they'll hear me sleepwalking. The animals treat me like one of the herd now.

li.label: kept my side deal
li.description: I made a private deal on the side, and the council let me keep the profit.

li.label: the colony's hero
li.description: The council says I'm the one who saved the colony. The story gets better every time I tell it.

li.label: no hero after all
li.description: I know what I did out there. The others remember it as a lot of shouting.

li.label: sent word home
li.description: I sent word home that I'm alive. I hope they sit down before they read it.

li.label: they moved on
li.description: I sent word home that I was alive. They wrote back that they've remarried, and asked me not to write again.

li.label: couldn't send word home
li.description: The people I left behind think I'm dead, and the council won't let me tell them otherwise.
